dedupe_keys.name: world bank city scan scripts for rapid city resilience assessments from global geospatial data

description: City Scan is the World Bank's workflow for a rapid assessment of the resilience challenges a city faces, built only from publicly available global geospatial datasets and open-source tools. The World Bank Group publishes the scripts and technical guidance in this repository; the outputs are the map packages, data and visualisations used in City Scan reports prepared for client cities. Coverage: any city worldwide, since every input is a global dataset; the repository lists its data sources in dated source tables. Modules process rasters for urban change, flooding, urban heat islands, landslides, earthquakes, imperviousness and desertification, and run road network analysis, accessibility mapping, vulnerability mapping and the relative wealth index for a city boundary. Format and access: Python and R scripts and notebooks on GitHub with map styling templates; inputs are fetched by the user from the listed global sources. Licence: MIT, free. Caveats: the repository is a collection of scripts, not a packaged tool, several modules expect the team's folder layout, and the underlying global layers are coarse for block-level decisions. Simulation uses: a quick first screen of hazard exposure and climate adaptation priorities for a city's buildings, roads and services before detailed modelling. Related records: the Copernicus Global Human Settlement Layer (data-copernicus-ghsl-built-up-population) and the Overture Maps buildings theme (data-overture-maps-buildings) are the kind of global layers it combines.
